The game, player conduct and the Rules
The central principles: play the course as you find it and the ball as it lies, act in the spirit of the game, and know the Rules.
The five areas of the course and the objects and conditions that can affect play.
Match play or stroke play, gross or net, and how the result is decided.
Which clubs and balls are allowed, how many clubs, and which devices may be used.
Too many clubs: in match play the match is adjusted by one hole per hole breached (max. two); in stroke play two strokes per hole (max. four).
When the round starts and ends, practice, pace of play and stopping play.
Unreasonable delay: one stroke, then the general penalty, then disqualification.
Starting from the teeing area, playing the same ball, the order of play and holing out.
Outside the teeing area: in match play the opponent may cancel the stroke; in stroke play two strokes and play again from inside it.
Ball search: finding and identifying ball
How you may search for your ball and identify it – and that there is no penalty for moving it accidentally while searching.
One stroke if you lift without marking or clean it more than needed.
Course played as it is found
You must not improve the conditions affecting your stroke – lie, area of stance or swing, line of play, relief area.
Ball played as it lies; ball at rest lifted or moved
Play the ball as it lies; what happens if it is lifted or moved by you, an opponent, an outside influence or natural forces.
Preparing for and making a stroke; advice and help; caddies
How to make a stroke, what advice is allowed, and what a caddie may do.
Ball in motion accidentally hits person, animal or object; deliberate actions to affect ball in motion
What happens when a moving ball hits someone or something – and that you must not deliberately stop or deflect it.
Play the ball out of the sand without testing it first.
On the green you may mark, lift and clean the ball, repair damage and remove sand – and decide about the flagstick.
Procedures for ball: marking, lifting and cleaning; replacing on spot; dropping in relief area; playing from wrong place
How to mark, lift, replace and drop a ball correctly – and what happens if you play from the wrong place.
Relief from loose impediments and movable obstructions (including ball or ball-marker helping or interfering with play)
Leaves, stones and twigs and movable objects like rakes or cans may be removed almost anywhere without penalty.
Relief from abnormal course conditions (including immovable obstructions), dangerous animal condition, embedded ball
Free relief from animal holes, ground under repair, immovable obstructions and temporary water – and for an embedded ball.
Water and other areas marked red or yellow: play it as it lies or take relief for one stroke.
Stroke-and-distance relief; ball lost or out of bounds; provisional ball
A lost ball or a ball out of bounds costs stroke and distance – save time with a provisional ball.
Anywhere except a penalty area you may declare your ball unplayable and take relief for one stroke.
Resolving rules issues during round; rulings by referee and committee
What to do when you are unsure how a rule applies – in stroke play you may play two balls.

Two against two per hole, left against right – the two scores of a team make one number.

Four players, two teams on every hole. The three pairings (A+B vs C+D, A+C vs B+D, A+D vs B+C) rotate hole by hole – on 18 holes each six times, on 9 holes three times – so everyone plays with everyone. The pairing of a hole can be changed.
The two scores of a team make a two-digit number, the lower one first: 6 and 5 = 56, 3 and 3 = 33.
Highest score 9 (if chosen): a 10 counts as 9. And a team without a par always puts the higher score first: bogey and double = 65, bogey and 10 = 95.
Without that: a score of 10 or more goes first: 10 and 4 = 104 (not 410).
Birdie −5 (if chosen): every birdie of a team takes 5 off its number, as long as nobody in the other team makes par – par and birdie = 34 − 5 = 29, two birdies = 33 − 10 = 23.
Eagle −10 (if chosen): an eagle or better takes 10 off instead of 5, on the same condition – eagle and par = 24 − 10 = 14.
The difference is the hole: 56 − 33 = 23. Each player of the lower team gets +23, each of the other −23 – all accounts add up to zero.
Press: only the player furthest behind, only at the start of a hole. The stake doubles and all points are halved – the money so far stays the same, the coming holes count double.
Highest stake: a step of the doubling chain (0.10 → 0.20 → 0.40 … 6.40 €, higher ones like 12.80 € typed in) or as a number of presses.
Gross or net: net gives the strokes of the playing handicap hole by hole after the stroke index (without one: evenly over the round).
